lower-left tip of the spray fan
middle of the rising spout, on its centreline
foot of the spout, just above the blowhole

myth: Orrun the Deep-Whale has been under both seas since before the first net was knotted. He carries the islands on his back, and when he rises to breathe he throws the sea up through his blowhole, and the spray climbs all the way to the Windward and stays there. It is why the fish come in. Aun saw the spout once, when his kite was too high and the string ran out, and he hung in it like wet cloth. He shouted up at the whale and asked where the wind stopped. Orrun did not answer. He only blew again, and the spray stood in the cold and did not fall. Hesk counts the drops, so we know the sea is still whole. Tavo, who cannot be bargained with, leaves the spout alone. So when the water rises white beside your boat, do not curse it. Count the drops, say Orrun's name, and tie your knot a little tighter.
verse:
Orrun breathes up white,
the spray stands in the cold sky,
count the drops, hold fast.
